about: Games that give your hands weight of their own, or can smooth or steady your aim themselves, so Decaffeinate's smoothing would add to theirs. 'weighted': the in-game hands or held weapons lag behind your real hands. 'smooths': the game has smoothing or steadying of its own. 'confidence': 'solid' when developer notes, reviews or someone who played it say so, and then a weighted game starts Decaf at 50% of the step until you set your own; 'players' when only community posts say it may, and then the Decaf page only says it may, in yellow. 'headset_checked' is true when someone has confirmed it in the game. Nobody has tried these with Decaf yet. Corrections welcome.

games.says: Physics weapons, tip-heavy swords.
Weapons have weight: swing too fast and the tip lags.
The hand follows yours on a spring, and weapons drag behind fast swings. The game's own spring and damper settings change it.
A physics body, and each avatar's strength sets how hard its hands can move things.
A physics body: heavy things move slowly and need two hands.
Melee weapons have simulated weight.
Held things have weight: heavy ones slow your hand, need two hands or fall.
Physics hands with a ghost hand showing where yours really are. Long guns wobble.

games.game: The Walking Dead: Saints & Sinners - Chapter 2: Retribution
games.says: The same physics hands. Heavy axes need two hands.

Smooths sniper rifles itself, with no way to turn it off, and steadies aim on the other hand's trigger.
Long Gun Stabilization steadies rifles while you hold the other hand's trigger, or always.
Players say hands track fine but guns lag on purpose to feel heavy. Its Interaction Weight setting turns that off.
Players say the stamina system slows punches below their real arm speed.
One player feels the arms slowed by simulated weight; another says it's only on contact.

Physics hands; a bug report says the hand was pulled down as if a pistol suddenly got heavier.
Players call the weapons floppy, flexing to give an illusion of mass.

Players say weapons flex, snap back to the controller and lag behind fast moves.
